Root cause fixed by commit `608e9e9a4ec4d2013faf1b8f9ecec09e90f131f2`. Vulnerable code keeps `orig_x` as a raw alias to the current `pdf_xref_entry` across the `pdf_load_obj_stm` call even though that helper can solidify and relocate the xref; the patch re-fetches the entry after the helper instead of reusing this stale pointer.

The annotations value from step 1 is still an indirect object, so `RESOLVE(obj)` dispatches into `pdf_resolve_indirect_chain` to load the referenced object before treating it as an array.
Indirect resolution converts the attacker-selected annotations reference into concrete xref object number 23, the object that `pdf_cache_object` will now fetch.
The object number from step 3 is handed to `pdf_cache_object`, moving the vulnerable path from indirect-object resolution into xref-entry caching.

Caching loads the current xref entry pointer for object 23. On the crashing path this entry is an unresolved object-stream member (`x->type == 'o'`) with no cached object yet, so later code will try to populate it from the object stream.
Inside the `x->type == 'o'` arm, the entry is still unresolved, so this branch is taken and `pdf_cache_object` enters the object-stream loading path instead of returning a cached object.

Before calling the helper, vulnerable code saves a second local alias to the same xref entry. That alias is meant to survive until the `fz_always` cleanup, but no refresh happens if the helper reorganizes the xref.

The object-stream loader reparses the containing object stream for the target object. While doing so it re-fetches member xref entries with the solidifying getter, so this call may return a current `x` from a reorganized xref while leaving `orig_x` unchanged.

While parsing the object stream, the helper re-fetches the member xref entry for the current object number with `pdf_get_xref_entry_no_null`. The saved ASan free stack identifies this exact getter call as the source operation that enters the solidifying xref lookup path.

The getter from step 9 calls `pdf_get_xref_entry(..., solidify_if_needed=1)`, so `pdf_get_xref_entry_aux` reaches `ensure_solid_xref` and frees the old xref-entry table before returning a replacement entry pointer. Because `orig_x` from step 7 still points into that table, this free turns it into a dangling pointer.

Sink. After step 8 returns to the `fz_always` cleanup, vulnerable code writes through `orig_x` instead of re-fetching the entry from the current xref layout. Because step 10 already freed the backing table, this is the saved 1-byte heap-use-after-free write at `pdf_cache_object:2504`.
